sc: Cold hands, capillary refill > 3 s, weak fast pulse → Shock: fluid bolus now
Shock, fever and purpura → Meningococcal sepsis: ceftriaxone
Shock with big liver, gallop, crackles, worse after a bolus → Stop fluids: inotropes
f: Emergency (ABCD signs: treat now) · priority (tiny baby < 2 mo, high fever, trauma, pallor, poisoning, pain, restless, referral, malnutrition, burns, oedema) · queue
Airway · Breathing (cyanosis, severe distress) · Circulation (cold hands + CRT > 3 s + weak fast pulse) · Coma, Convulsions · Dehydration (severe)
Airway, oxygen · shock: 10–20 ml/kg saline/RL (SAM: 15 ml/kg over 1 h) · glucose 10% dextrose 5 ml/kg · fits: rectal diazepam 0.5 mg/kg
Antibiotics within 1 hour · reassess after each bolus · fluid-refractory: adrenaline/noradrenaline
Commonest arrest rhythm: asystole/PEA (hypoxic) · 5 rescue breaths, 15 : 2, 100–120/min · adrenaline 10 µg/kg · VF: 4 J/kg
trap: Shocked child with SAM: slower, smaller fluid (heart failure risk) · fitting child with no glucometer → give dextrose · AVPU = P or U means coma
